e-7053.knowledge_point: Computing the Integral of an Exponential Expression Using Integration by Parts Twice
e-7053.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u={t}^{2}+1\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}=2t, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}={e}^{2t+1}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t=\int {e}^{2t+1}\,\text{d}t=\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({t}^{2}+1){e}^{2t+1}\,\text{d}t & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =({t}^{2}+1)(\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{2})-\int (\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{2})(2t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{({t}^{2}+1){e}^{2t+1}}{2}-\int t\,{e}^{2t+1}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\displaystyle\int t\,e^{2t+1}\,\textrm{d}t.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=t\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}=1 \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}={e}^{2t+1}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t=\int {e}^{2t+1}\,\text{d}t=\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int t\,{e}^{2t+1}\,\text{d}t & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =(t)(\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{2})-\int (\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{2})(1)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{t\,{e}^{2t+1}}{2}-\frac{1}{2}\int {e}^{2t+1}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{t\,{e}^{2t+1}}{2}-\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{4}+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is a constant. 

So, we get that the indefinite integral is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({t}^{2}+1){e}^{2t+1}\,\text{d}t & =\frac{({t}^{2}+1){e}^{2t+1}}{2}-\int t\,{e}^{2t+1}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{({t}^{2}+1){e}^{2t+1}}{2}-(\frac{t\,{e}^{2t+1}}{2}-\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{4}+D) \\  & =\frac{({t}^{2}+1){e}^{2t+1}}{2}-\frac{t\,{e}^{2t+1}}{2}+\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{4}-D \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{4}(2{t}^{2}-2t+3)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C = -{D}.$ 

Finally then, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}({t}^{2}+1){e}^{2t+1}\,\text{d}t & ={[\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{4}(2{t}^{2}-2t+3)]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(\frac{{e}^{2(1)+1}}{4}(2(1)^{2}-2(1)+3))-(\frac{{e}^{2(0)+1}}{4}(2(0)^{2}-2(0)+3)) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{3}}{4}(2-2+3)-\frac{e}{4}(0-0+3) \\  & =\frac{3{e}^{3}}{4}-\frac{3e}{4} \\  & =\frac{3{e}^{3}-3e}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

e-495.knowledge_point: Computing the Integral of a Trigonometric Expression Using Integration by Parts Twice
e-495.worked_solution:
In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u={x}^{2} & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2x\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x) & \,⟹\,v=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\text{d}x=\frac{1}{3}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\text{d}x \\  & =({x}^{2})(\frac{1}{3}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x))-\int (\frac{1}{3}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x))2x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-\frac{2}{3}\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, we use integration by parts to evaluate $\displaystyle \int x\sin(3x) \textrm{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x) & \,⟹\,v=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\text{d}x=-\,\frac{1}{3}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\text{d}x \\  & =x(-\,\frac{1}{3}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x))-\int (-\,\frac{1}{3}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x))\cdot 1\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\,\frac{1}{3}\,x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+\frac{1}{3}\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\text{d}x \\  & =-\,\frac{1}{3}\,x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+\frac{1}{3}(\frac{1}{3}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x))+{C}_{1} \\  & =-\,\frac{1}{3}\,x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+\frac{1}{9}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+{C}_{1}\,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C_1$ is a constant of integration.
So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{3}{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-\frac{2}{3}\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-\frac{2}{3}(-\,\frac{1}{3}\,x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+\frac{1}{9}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+{C}_{1}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+\frac{2}{9}x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)-\frac{2}{27}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-\frac{2{C}_{1}}{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{27}((9{x}^{2}-2)\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+6x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x))+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C = -\dfrac{2C_1}{3}.$

e-496.knowledge_point: Computing the Integral of a Logarithmic Expression Using Integration by Parts Twice
e-496.worked_solution:
We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{2} & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{x}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=32{x}^{3} & \,⟹\,v=\int 32{x}^{3}\text{d}x=8{x}^{4}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 32{x}^{3}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{2}\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\text{d}x \\  & ={(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}(8{x}^{4})-\int (8{x}^{4})(\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{x})\text{d}x \\  & =8{x}^{4}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}-16\int {x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\displaystyle\int {x^3\ln(x)} \textrm{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x) & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={x}^{3} & \,⟹\,v=\int {x}^{3}\text{d}x=\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)(\frac{{x}^{4}}{4})-\int (\frac{{x}^{4}}{4})(\frac{1}{x})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)}{4}-\frac{1}{4}\int {x}^{3}\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)}{4}-\frac{{x}^{4}}{16}+{C}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

where $C_1$ is an integral constant. So, we get that the indefinite integral is

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 32{x}^{3}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{2}\text{d}x & =8{x}^{4}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}-16\int {x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\text{d}x \\  & =8{x}^{4}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}-16(\frac{{x}^{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)}{4}-\frac{{x}^{4}}{16}+{C}_{1}) \\  & =8{x}^{4}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}-4{x}^{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)+{x}^{4}-16{C}_{1} \\  & ={x}^{4}(8{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}-4\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)+1)+C\,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C = -4C_1.$ Finally then, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}32{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\text{d}x & ={{x}^{4}(8{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}-4\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)+1)|}_{1}^{e} \\  & =[(e)^{4}(8{(\operatorname{ln}⁡(e))}^{2}-4\operatorname{ln}⁡(e)+1)]-[(1)^{4}(8{(\operatorname{ln}⁡(1))}^{2}-4\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)+1)] \\  & =[{e}^{4}(8-4+1)]-1 \\  & =5{e}^{4}-1.\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 5
?

Calculate the integral ∫(4x2+1)e2xdx.

a
e2x2(2x2−2x+1)+C
b
e2x2(4x2−2x−3)+C
c
e2x2(4x2−4x+3)+C
d
e2x2(x2−2x+3)+C
e
e2x2(2x2+4x+1)+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Integration by parts twice gives e^{2x}(2x^2-2x+3/2)+C, matching option c. Differentiating it yields e^{2x}[(4x^2-4x+3)+(4x-2)]=(4x^2+1)e^{2x}.

after.name: Question 5
after.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=4{x}^{2}+1\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=8x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={e}^{2x}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int {e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x=\frac{{e}^{2x}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (4{x}^{2}+1){e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(4{x}^{2}+1)(\frac{{e}^{2x}}{2})-\int (\frac{{e}^{2x}}{2})(8x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{(4{x}^{2}+1){e}^{2x}}{2}-4\int x{e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\int x{e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1 \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={e}^{2x}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int {e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x=\frac{{e}^{2x}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x(\frac{{e}^{2x}}{2})-\int (\frac{{e}^{2x}}{2})(1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x{e}^{2x}}{2}-\frac{1}{2}\int {e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x{e}^{2x}}{2}-\frac{{e}^{2x}}{4}+D \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2x}}{4}(2x-1)+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant.

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (4{x}^{2}+1){e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{(4{x}^{2}+1){e}^{2x}}{2}-4(\frac{{e}^{2x}}{4}(2x-1)+D) \\  & =\frac{(4{x}^{2}+1){e}^{2x}}{2}-{e}^{2x}(2x-1)-4D \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2x}}{2}(4{x}^{2}-4x+3)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-4D.$

after.html:
Question 5
?

Calculate the integral ∫(4x2+1)e2xdx.

a
e2x2(2x2−2x+1)+C
b
e2x2(4x2−2x−3)+C
c
e2x2(4x2−4x+3)+C
d
e2x2(x2−2x+3)+C
e
e2x2(2x2+4x+1)+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We need to use integration by parts.

In this case, we define u=4x2+1⟹dudx=8xdvdx=e2x⟹v=∫dvdxdx=∫e2xdx=e2x2.

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get ∫(4x2+1)e2xdx=∫udvdxdx=uv−∫vdudxdx=(4x2+1)(e2x2)−∫(e2x2)(8x)dx=(4x2+1)e2x2−4∫xe2xdx.

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate ∫xe2xdx. We take

u=x⟹dudx=1dvdx=e2x⟹v=∫dvdxdx=∫e2xdx=e2x2.

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives ∫xe2xdx=∫udvdxdx=uv−∫vdudxdx=x(e2x2)−∫(e2x2)(1)dx=xe2x2−12∫e2xdx=xe2x2−e2x4+D=e2x4(2x−1)+D, where D is an integral constant.

So we have ∫(4x2+1)e2xdx=(4x2+1)e2x2−4(e2x4(2x−1)+D)=(4x2+1)e2x2−e2x(2x−1)−4D=e2x2(4x2−4x+3)+C, where C=−4D.

content.knowledge_point: Computing the Integral of an Exponential Expression Using Integration by Parts Twice
content.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=4{x}^{2}+1\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=8x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={e}^{2x}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int {e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x=\frac{{e}^{2x}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (4{x}^{2}+1){e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(4{x}^{2}+1)(\frac{{e}^{2x}}{2})-\int (\frac{{e}^{2x}}{2})(8x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{(4{x}^{2}+1){e}^{2x}}{2}-4\int x{e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\int x{e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1 \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={e}^{2x}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int {e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x=\frac{{e}^{2x}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x(\frac{{e}^{2x}}{2})-\int (\frac{{e}^{2x}}{2})(1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x{e}^{2x}}{2}-\frac{1}{2}\int {e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x{e}^{2x}}{2}-\frac{{e}^{2x}}{4}+D \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2x}}{4}(2x-1)+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant.

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (4{x}^{2}+1){e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{(4{x}^{2}+1){e}^{2x}}{2}-4(\frac{{e}^{2x}}{4}(2x-1)+D) \\  & =\frac{(4{x}^{2}+1){e}^{2x}}{2}-{e}^{2x}(2x-1)-4D \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2x}}{2}(4{x}^{2}-4x+3)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-4D.$

∫0π/24t2sin⁡tdt=
Submit

decision.explanation: Integration by parts twice gives the antiderivative -4t^2 cos(t)+8t sin(t)+8 cos(t). At π/2 it equals 4π, and at 0 it equals 8, so the integral is 4π-8.

after.name: Question 6
after.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=4{t}^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}=8t \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=\operatorname{sin}⁡t\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t=-\operatorname{cos}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 4{t}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =(4{t}^{2})(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)(8t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =-4{t}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t+8\int t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, we use integration by parts to evaluate $\int t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=t & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}=1\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=\operatorname{cos}⁡t & \,⟹\,v=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡t\text{d}t=\operatorname{sin}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =t\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\int \operatorname{sin}⁡t\,dt \\  & =t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant. 

So, we get that the indefinite integral is

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 4{t}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t & =-4{t}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t+8\int t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & =-4{t}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t+8(t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t+D) \\  & =-4{t}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t+8t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+8\operatorname{cos}⁡t+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=8D.$

Finally, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}4{t}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t & ={[-4{t}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t+8t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+8\operatorname{cos}⁡t]}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =(0+8(\frac{\pi }{2})(1)+0)-(0+0+8) \\  & =4\pi -8 \\  & =4\pi -8\end{aligned}
$$

We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=4{x}^{2}+2\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=8x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡x\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{sin}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (4{x}^{2}+2)\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(4{x}^{2}+2)(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)-\int (\operatorname{sin}⁡x)(8x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =(4{x}^{2}+2)\operatorname{sin}⁡x-8\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, we use integration by parts to evaluate $\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡x & \,⟹\,v=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x=-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-x\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\,dx \\  & =-x\operatorname{cos}⁡x+\operatorname{sin}⁡x+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant. 

So, we get that the indefinite integral is

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (4{x}^{2}+2)\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =(4{x}^{2}+2)\operatorname{sin}⁡x-8\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =(4{x}^{2}+2)\operatorname{sin}⁡x-8(-x\operatorname{cos}⁡x+\operatorname{sin}⁡x+D) \\  & =(4{x}^{2}+2)\operatorname{sin}⁡x+8x\operatorname{cos}⁡x-8\operatorname{sin}⁡x+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-8D.$

Finally, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(4{x}^{2}+2)\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x & ={[(4{x}^{2}+2)\operatorname{sin}⁡x+8x\operatorname{cos}⁡x-8\operatorname{sin}⁡x]}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =((4{(\frac{\pi }{2})}^{2}+2)\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{\pi }{2}+8(\frac{\pi }{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{\pi }{2}-8\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{\pi }{2})-(2\operatorname{sin}⁡0+8(0)\operatorname{cos}⁡0-8\operatorname{sin}⁡0) \\  & =({\pi }^{2}+2+0-8)-0 \\  & ={\pi }^{2}-6 \\  & ={\pi }^{2}-6\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Take u=x² and dv=sin(3x) dx, so du=2x dx and v=-cos(3x)/3. Integration by parts gives -x²cos(3x)/3+(2/3)∫x cos(3x) dx, which is option d.

after.name: Question 9
after.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts. 

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u={x}^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x=-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({x}^{2})(-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3})-\int (-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3})(2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3}+\frac{2}{3}\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Computing the Integral of a Trigonometric Expression Using Integration by Parts Twice
content.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts. 

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u={x}^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x=-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({x}^{2})(-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3})-\int (-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3})(2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3}+\frac{2}{3}\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Choose u=4x²+1 and dv=sin(3x) dx. Then du=8x dx and v=-cos(3x)/3. Thus uv-∫v du gives -(4x²+1)cos(3x)/3+(8/3)∫x cos(3x) dx, matching option b.

after.name: Question 10
after.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts. 

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=4{x}^{2}+1\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=8x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x=-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (4{x}^{2}+1)\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(4{x}^{2}+1)(-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3})-\int (-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3})(8x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{(4{x}^{2}+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3}+\frac{8}{3}\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Computing the Integral of a Trigonometric Expression Using Integration by Parts Twice
content.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts. 

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=4{x}^{2}+1\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=8x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x=-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (4{x}^{2}+1)\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(4{x}^{2}+1)(-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3})-\int (-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3})(8x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{(4{x}^{2}+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3}+\frac{8}{3}\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Use log₃(x)=ln(x)/ln(3). Integration by parts twice gives the antiderivative x²[2(ln(x))²-2ln(x)+1]/(ln(3))². Evaluating at e and 1 gives (e²-1)/(ln(3))², matching option c.

after.name: Question 11
after.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=({log}_{3}⁡x)^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2{log}_{3}⁡x}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=4x\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int 4x\,\text{d}x=2{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 4x({log}_{3}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={({log}_{3}⁡x)}^{2}(2{x}^{2})-\int (2{x}^{2})(\frac{2{log}_{3}⁡x}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =2{x}^{2}({log}_{3}⁡x)^{2}-\frac{4}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int x{log}_{3}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\int x{log}_{3}⁡(x)\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{3}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=x\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int x\,\text{d}x=\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{log}_{3}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({log}_{3}⁡x)(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})-\int (\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})(\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}{log}_{3}⁡x}{2}-\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}{log}_{3}⁡x}{2}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{4\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is a constant. 

So, we get that the indefinite integral is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 4x({log}_{3}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & =2{x}^{2}({log}_{3}⁡x)^{2}-\frac{4}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}(\frac{{x}^{2}{log}_{3}⁡x}{2}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{4\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+D) \\  & =2{x}^{2}({log}_{3}⁡x)^{2}-\frac{2{x}^{2}{log}_{3}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+\frac{{x}^{2}}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}+C \\  & =\frac{2{x}^{2}{ln}^{2}⁡x}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}-\frac{2{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}+\frac{{x}^{2}}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}(2{ln}^{2}⁡x-2\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-\frac{4D}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}.$ 

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{3}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}.$

Finally then, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}4x({log}_{3}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & ={[\frac{{x}^{2}}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}(2{ln}^{2}⁡x-2\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1)]}_{1}^{e} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2}}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}(2{ln}^{2}⁡e-2\operatorname{ln}⁡e+1)-\frac{{1}^{2}}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}(2{ln}^{2}⁡1-2\operatorname{ln}⁡1+1) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2}}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}(2-2+1)-\frac{1}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}(0-0+1) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2}-1}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define u=(log3⁡x)2⟹dudx=2log3⁡xxln⁡3dvdx=4x⟹v=∫dvdxdx=∫4xdx=2x2.

This gives ∫4x(log3⁡x)2dx=∫udvdxdx=uv−∫vdudxdx=(log3⁡x)2(2x2)−∫(2x2)(2log3⁡xxln⁡3)dx=2x2(log3⁡x)2−4ln⁡3∫xlog3⁡(x)dx.

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate ∫xlog3⁡(x)dx. We take

u=log3⁡(x)⟹dudx=1xln⁡3dvdx=x⟹v=∫dvdxdx=∫xdx=x22.

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives ∫xlog3⁡xdx=∫udvdxdx=uv−∫vdudxdx=(log3⁡x)(x22)−∫(x22)(1xln⁡3)dx=x2log3⁡x2−12ln⁡3∫xdx=x2log3⁡x2−x24ln⁡3+D, where D is a constant.

So, we get that the indefinite integral is ∫4x(log3⁡x)2dx=2x2(log3⁡x)2−4ln⁡3(x2log3⁡x2−x24ln⁡3+D)=2x2(log3⁡x)2−2x2log3⁡xln⁡3+x2ln2⁡3+C=2x2ln2⁡xln2⁡3−2x2ln⁡xln2⁡3+x2ln2⁡3+C=x2ln2⁡3(2ln2⁡x−2ln⁡x+1)+C, where C=−4Dln⁡3.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula log3⁡x=ln⁡xln⁡3.

Finally then, we can work out the definite integral: ∫1e4x(log3⁡x)2dx=[x2ln2⁡3(2ln2⁡x−2ln⁡x+1)]1e=e2ln2⁡3(2ln2⁡e−2ln⁡e+1)−12ln2⁡3(2ln2⁡1−2ln⁡1+1)=e2ln2⁡3(2−2+1)−1ln2⁡3(0−0+1)=e2−1ln2⁡3.

content.knowledge_point: Computing the Integral of a Logarithmic Expression Using Integration by Parts Twice
content.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=({log}_{3}⁡x)^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2{log}_{3}⁡x}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=4x\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int 4x\,\text{d}x=2{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 4x({log}_{3}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={({log}_{3}⁡x)}^{2}(2{x}^{2})-\int (2{x}^{2})(\frac{2{log}_{3}⁡x}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =2{x}^{2}({log}_{3}⁡x)^{2}-\frac{4}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int x{log}_{3}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\int x{log}_{3}⁡(x)\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{3}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=x\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int x\,\text{d}x=\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{log}_{3}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({log}_{3}⁡x)(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})-\int (\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})(\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}{log}_{3}⁡x}{2}-\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}{log}_{3}⁡x}{2}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{4\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is a constant. 

So, we get that the indefinite integral is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 4x({log}_{3}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & =2{x}^{2}({log}_{3}⁡x)^{2}-\frac{4}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}(\frac{{x}^{2}{log}_{3}⁡x}{2}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{4\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+D) \\  & =2{x}^{2}({log}_{3}⁡x)^{2}-\frac{2{x}^{2}{log}_{3}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+\frac{{x}^{2}}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}+C \\  & =\frac{2{x}^{2}{ln}^{2}⁡x}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}-\frac{2{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}+\frac{{x}^{2}}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}(2{ln}^{2}⁡x-2\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-\frac{4D}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}.$ 

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{3}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}.$

Finally then, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}4x({log}_{3}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & ={[\frac{{x}^{2}}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}(2{ln}^{2}⁡x-2\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1)]}_{1}^{e} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2}}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}(2{ln}^{2}⁡e-2\operatorname{ln}⁡e+1)-\frac{{1}^{2}}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}(2{ln}^{2}⁡1-2\operatorname{ln}⁡1+1) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2}}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}(2-2+1)-\frac{1}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}(0-0+1) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2}-1}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1))^{2} & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)}{x+1}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=27(x+1)^{2} & \,⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int 27(x+1)^{2}\,\text{d}x=9(x+1)^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 27(x+1)^{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1))^{2}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1))}^{2}(9(x+1)^{3})-\int (9(x+1)^{3})(\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)}{x+1})\,\text{d}x \\  & =9(x+1)^{3}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1))}^{2}-18\int (x+1)^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 15
?

Calculate the integral ∫(log4⁡x)2dx.

a
 x(log4⁡x)2+2log4⁡(x)+C
b
x((log4⁡x)2−2log4⁡(x)ln⁡4+2ln2⁡4)+C
c
x((log4⁡x)2+log4⁡(x)ln⁡4+1ln2⁡4)+C
d
x(log4⁡(x)+2ln2⁡4)+C
e
x(log4⁡(x)−1ln2⁡4)+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Since log₄(x)=ln(x)/ln(4), integrating by parts twice gives x[(ln(x))²-2ln(x)+2]/(ln(4))²+C. Rewriting in base 4 matches option b.

after.name: Question 15
after.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=({log}_{4}⁡x)^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2{log}_{4}⁡x}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡4} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \,\text{d}x=x.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({log}_{4}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={({log}_{4}⁡x)}^{2}(x)-\int (x)(\frac{2{log}_{4}⁡x}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡4})\,\text{d}x \\  & =x{({log}_{4}⁡x)}^{2}-\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\int {log}_{4}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate  $\int {log}_{4}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{4}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡4} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \,\text{d}x=x.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {log}_{4}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({log}_{4}⁡(x))(x)-\int (x)(\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡4})\,\text{d}x \\  & =x{log}_{4}⁡(x)-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\int \,\text{d}x \\  & =x{log}_{4}⁡(x)-\frac{x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant.

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({log}_{4}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & =x{({log}_{4}⁡x)}^{2}-\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}(x{log}_{4}⁡(x)-\frac{x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+D) \\  & =x{({log}_{4}⁡x)}^{2}-\frac{2x{log}_{4}⁡(x)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+\frac{2x}{{ln}^{2}⁡4}-\frac{2D}{\operatorname{ln}⁡4} \\  & =x({({log}_{4}⁡x)}^{2}-\frac{2{log}_{4}⁡(x)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+\frac{2}{{ln}^{2}⁡4})+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-\frac{2D}{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}.$

after.html:
Question 15
?

Calculate the integral ∫(log4⁡x)2dx.

a
 x(log4⁡x)2+2log4⁡(x)+C
b
x((log4⁡x)2−2log4⁡(x)ln⁡4+2ln2⁡4)+C
c
x((log4⁡x)2+log4⁡(x)ln⁡4+1ln2⁡4)+C
d
x(log4⁡(x)+2ln2⁡4)+C
e
x(log4⁡(x)−1ln2⁡4)+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We need to use integration by parts.

In this case, we define u=(log4⁡x)2⟹dudx=2log4⁡xxln⁡4dvdx=1⟹v=∫dvdxdx=∫dx=x.

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get ∫(log4⁡x)2dx=∫udvdxdx=uv−∫vdudxdx=(log4⁡x)2(x)−∫(x)(2log4⁡xxln⁡4)dx=x(log4⁡x)2−2ln⁡4∫log4⁡(x)dx.

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate ∫log4⁡(x)dx. We take u=log4⁡(x)⟹dudx=1xln⁡4dvdx=1⟹v=∫dvdxdx=∫dx=x.

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives ∫log4⁡(x)dx=∫udvdxdx=uv−∫vdudxdx=(log4⁡(x))(x)−∫(x)(1xln⁡4)dx=xlog4⁡(x)−1ln⁡4∫dx=xlog4⁡(x)−xln⁡4+D, where D is an integral constant.

So we have ∫(log4⁡x)2dx=x(log4⁡x)2−2ln⁡4(xlog4⁡(x)−xln⁡4+D)=x(log4⁡x)2−2xlog4⁡(x)ln⁡4+2xln2⁡4−2Dln⁡4=x((log4⁡x)2−2log4⁡(x)ln⁡4+2ln2⁡4)+C, where C=−2Dln⁡4.

content.knowledge_point: Computing the Integral of a Logarithmic Expression Using Integration by Parts Twice
content.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=({log}_{4}⁡x)^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2{log}_{4}⁡x}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡4} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \,\text{d}x=x.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({log}_{4}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={({log}_{4}⁡x)}^{2}(x)-\int (x)(\frac{2{log}_{4}⁡x}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡4})\,\text{d}x \\  & =x{({log}_{4}⁡x)}^{2}-\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\int {log}_{4}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate  $\int {log}_{4}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{4}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡4} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \,\text{d}x=x.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {log}_{4}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({log}_{4}⁡(x))(x)-\int (x)(\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡4})\,\text{d}x \\  & =x{log}_{4}⁡(x)-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\int \,\text{d}x \\  & =x{log}_{4}⁡(x)-\frac{x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant.

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({log}_{4}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & =x{({log}_{4}⁡x)}^{2}-\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}(x{log}_{4}⁡(x)-\frac{x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+D) \\  & =x{({log}_{4}⁡x)}^{2}-\frac{2x{log}_{4}⁡(x)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+\frac{2x}{{ln}^{2}⁡4}-\frac{2D}{\operatorname{ln}⁡4} \\  & =x({({log}_{4}⁡x)}^{2}-\frac{2{log}_{4}⁡(x)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+\frac{2}{{ln}^{2}⁡4})+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-\frac{2D}{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}.$
